Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

afford verb

also can afford, can’t afford, affordable, I can’t afford it, be able to pay

classical

Plaut. Trin. 564: vērum quod det nōn habet, but he can’t afford it
Plaut. Asin. 242: sī nōn est quod dēs, if you can’t pay

habēre quod dēs

phrase: habēre with a relative clause in the subjunctive

afford, have the money to pay; literally, have something to give

Latin says what one has to give: nōn habeō quod dem, I can’t afford it; or with est, mihi nōn est quod dem (Plaut. Trin. 761). What one can afford is one’s facultātēs, one’s means (see resources): each gave prō facultāte, as he could afford (Suet. Aug. 57.2).

Other words

  • solvendō esse — be able to pay (what is owed)

    phrase: gerund in the dative with esse · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.8.2: cum solvendō cīvitātēs nōn essent, when the towns could not afford to pay; Cic. Att. 13.10.3: solvendō enim nōn erat, for he could not pay his debts

    Of debts and bills; nōn esse solvendō, to be unable to pay, insolvent.

Examples

  • Quid cēnsēs? homōst: volt fierī līber, vērum quod det nōn habet.

    What do you think? He’s only human: he wants to be freed, but he hasn’t the money to pay for it.Plaut. Trin. 563–564

  • multārum cīvitātum prīncipēs ad mē dētulērunt sūmptūs dēcernī lēgātīs nimis magnōs, cum solvendō cīvitātēs nōn essent

    the leading men of many towns told me that far too much was being voted for the envoys’ expenses, when the towns could not afford to payCic. Fam. 3.8.2

See also price, expensive, cheap, resources, pay.
